description: One SEO element repaired or improved per iteration, evidence-first: every story is verified against the actual prerendered output in website/dist/client, not against intent. Work that does not fit a single iteration is written down here rather than half-attempted. Strategy context lives in pSEO.md and docs/SEO_STRATEGY.md.

userStories.title: Unbreak the website production build so SEO changes can actually deploy
userStories.description: As the site owner, I want `npm run build` to succeed so that Cloudflare Pages keeps deploying, because every SEO surface this repo owns (prerendered HTML, canonicals, JSON-LD, sitemap.xml, the IndexNow ping) is emitted by that one script.
acceptanceCriteria: `npx tsc -b` exits 0 in website/
`npm run build` exits 0 and prerenders every route
dist/client/sitemap.xml is regenerated and non-empty
A GitHub Actions workflow gates website/** pull requests on the build
userStories.notes: Root cause: src/test/fonts.test.ts (added by US-WEB020) uses node:fs and __dirname, but tsconfig.app.json includes src/ with types ['vite/client'] only, so tsc -b exited 2 and the whole build script stopped before vite build. Fixed by giving the tests their own project (tsconfig.test.json) and excluding src/test from the app project. Guarded by .github/workflows/website-check.yml.

userStories.title: Make website eslint clean and add it to the CI gate
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want `npm run lint` green and gated so that the website check workflow can enforce it the way edge-functions-check.yml enforces deno lint.
acceptanceCriteria: `npm run lint` exits 0 in website/
No rule is disabled wholesale to get there — each error is fixed or suppressed inline with a reason
A `Lint` step is added back to .github/workflows/website-check.yml and passes
userStories.notes: 9 errors / 10 warnings today, concentrated in react-hooks/set-state-in-effect (Blog.tsx, BlogPost.tsx, admin/*) and @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any (utils/analytics.ts). The set-state-in-effect ones are real refactors of the blog data-loading path, not cosmetic — likely its own iteration.

userStories.title: Stop leaking a JSX comment block into every page's <head>
userStories.description: As a crawler, I want the document head to contain only markup so that the shipped HTML is valid and not padded with source commentary.
acceptanceCriteria: No `{/*` sequence appears in any file under dist/client
The explanatory prose survives as a real source comment in pages/+onRenderHtml.tsx or as an HTML comment
fonts.test.ts still passes
userStories.notes: Root cause: STATIC_HEAD in pages/+onRenderHtml.tsx is a template literal in a .tsx file, so the JSX comment written inside it was copied byte-for-byte into the head of all 34 prerendered documents (940 bytes each, 31960 total). The prose now lives in a real TypeScript comment above the literal. Guarded twice: src/test/head.test.ts asserts the literal carries no JSX comment syntax, and website-check.yml greps the emitted dist/client HTML, which is what crawlers actually read.

userStories.title: Remove or configure the placeholder Cloudflare Insights beacon
userStories.description: As a visitor, I don't want a third-party script requested on every page with a token that was never filled in, because it costs a connection on the LCP path and returns nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: No script tag ships with a literal PLACEHOLDER/YOUR_* token
Either a real token is injected from an env var at build time, or the beacon is removed
If it stays, it is gated behind the same consent flow as GA4 (src/lib/consent.ts)
userStories.notes: The tag now renders only when VITE_CF_ANALYTICS_TOKEN holds a 32-hex token, and the token is validated before interpolation because it lands inside a JSON attribute. Verified across three builds: no token -> 0 beacons, real token -> 34 beacons with the token intact, hostile token -> 0 beacons plus a build warning. OWNER ACTION: /privacy and /cookies tell visitors Cloudflare Web Analytics is in use; that is only true once the token is set in the Cloudflare Pages build environment.

userStories.title: Complete the social card contract: image dimensions, type, and twitter:site
userStories.description: As a link shared into Slack/X/iMessage, I want a fully-specified card so previews render large instead of falling back to a small thumbnail while the image is fetched.
acceptanceCriteria: og:image:width, og:image:height and og:image:type emitted alongside og:image
Dimensions match the real og-image.png rather than being assumed
SEO.tsx accepts an optional per-page image so comparison and /what-to-do pages can override the sitewide default
userStories.notes: website/src/components/SEO.tsx ships one hard-coded og-image.png for all 33 indexable URLs.

userStories.title: Land the search-console verification tokens
userStories.description: As the site owner, I want Google, Bing and Yandex ownership verified so that indexing coverage and query data are observable at all.
acceptanceCriteria: Verification meta tags emitted from env vars, or ownership verified via DNS and the commented block deleted
No PASTE_* placeholder remains in pages/+onRenderHtml.tsx
userStories.notes: The three tags are commented out with PASTE_*_TOKEN placeholders. Real tokens are secrets and are not in this repo — this story needs values from the owner, so it is blocked on input rather than on effort.

userStories.title: Typecheck the pages/ directory
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want tsc to cover pages/ so that the file producing every page's <head> is not the one file nobody typechecks.
acceptanceCriteria: pages/**/*.ts(x) is included in a TypeScript project reachable from tsconfig.json
`npx tsc -b` exits 0 with it included
vike/types and vite/client types resolve there
userStories.notes: tsconfig.app.json includes only src/, and tsconfig.node.json only vite.config.ts, so pages/+onRenderHtml.tsx, +Page.tsx, +config.ts and +onBeforePrerenderStart.ts are wholly unchecked today. That is the SSR entry point and the source of every canonical, JSON-LD block and meta tag. Adding it may surface a batch of pre-existing errors, which is why it is its own story.
